cues.text: Talk about one other person or thing: he, she or it.
Add s to a doing word like read or play.
Person, Verb, Question, Short answer.
I, you, we, they, read, Do you read, Yes, I do.
he, she, it, reads, Does he read, Yes, he does.
Put does not or doesn't before the plain verb to say no.
Sentence, With not, Short form.
He reads, He does not read, He doesn't read.
She plays, She does not play, She doesn't play.
Rule: Use reads with he, she and it.
After does and doesn't, use read with no s.
Ben reads at home every day.
He reads after dinner too.
She plays music after school.
The cat sleeps in the room.
It sleeps on the bed.
Does Emma read at school?
Yes, she does.
Ben doesn't eat fish for lunch.

Watch out:

Wrong: He is reads at home.
Right: He reads at home.
Use reads alone.
Do not put is before it.
Wrong: Does Ben reads?
Right: Does Ben read?
Does shows he, so drop the s.
Wrong: She don't like milk.
Right: She doesn't like milk.
Use doesn't with he, she and it.
These four words tell how often someone does a routine.
Word, How often, Example.
always, every time, She always reads at night.
usually, on most days, He usually walks to school.
sometimes, on some days, not every day, We sometimes play together.
never, not at any time, They never eat late.
Put these words before a doing word.
Put them after am, is and are.
Verb, Place, Example.
doing word, before the verb, Ben usually walks home.
be, after am, is, are, Emma is always ready.
Rule: Put these words before a doing word.
Put them after am, is and are.
Sometimes can also start a sentence.
Ask with How often does.
She always reads before bed.
Ben usually helps at home.
I am usually ready early.
We are never late for school.
Sometimes we walk in the park.
How often does he read?
He reads every day.

Watch out:

Wrong: He reads always at home.
Right: He always reads at home.
Put always before the doing word.
Wrong: She always is ready.
Right: She is always ready.
Put always after is.
Look at the back of a verb.
Choose the ending for he, she or it.
Rule, Example.
Most words: add s, read, reads.
Ends in ch, sh, ss, x, zz: add es, watch, watches.
a, e, i, o, u + y: add s, play, plays.
Other letter + y: y, ies, study, studies.
Special words, have, has.
Special words, go, goes.
Special words, do, does.
Look at reads.
Write r-e-a-d, then add s.
Look at studies.
Before y is d, not a vowel.
So y changes to ies.
Rule: Add s to most verbs.
Add es after ch, sh, ss, x and zz.
Keep y after a, e, i, o, u.
Change y to ies after other letters.
He watches TV after dinner.
Emma washes cups in the kitchen.
My brother plays games on Friday.
She studies English in the evening.
He has a new pen.
She goes home at four.

Watch out:

Wrong: He studys English.
Right: He studies English.
Before y is d, so change y to ies.
Wrong: She watchs TV.
Right: She watches TV.
After ch, add es.
Wrong: It haves four legs.
Right: It has four legs.
Have changes to has.
